notes.title: Load combination, P7 (10/05)
notes.text: She says "one load combination", 1.2D + 1.6L (R3 above), and that is the number for any problem with enough live load. With only D and L the calculators also form 1.4D (ASCE 7 combination 1, line 1 of her week-1 slide, listed on this page) and print the LARGER: when L is less than D/8 the 1.4D value governs (D 100 alone: 1.4D = 140, 1.2D + 1.6L = 120). Both lines are printed in the work, so her number is always on the page. A load the problem gives already factored is never factored again, and with a factored load present only 1.2D + 1.6L is formed.

notes.title: Her practice, from her own solution sheets (read 10/04, `extracted/hw-solutions/findings.md`):
notes.text: reads Table 4-14 at a whole KL/r -- usually the next row UP (129.23 -> 130; 17.14 ft -> 18 ft; "just round up" on 9/30), once the nearest (95.05 -> 95), once the average of two rows (61.5); a problem's "Lc" is the MEMBER length and she applies K to it (6-7b: 0.8 x 25 = 20 ft); two live loads on a floor -> the larger; roof live load factored 1.6 like floor live; self-weight added after choosing; girder load = 2 x the beam reaction when beams frame in from both sides.

notes: (Lr or S or R) = the LARGEST of the three; the answer names which one was used.
L* = 0.5 L, allowed when the occupancy live load is less than or equal to 100 psf, except garages and places of public assembly (1.0 L there). Her wk3-4 slide: 277 k = 1.2(65) + 1.0(144) + 0.5(110).

Combinations 3, 4 and 6 use the TOWARD value of W / E. Combinations 5 and 7 subtract the REVERSE value when one is given (textbook Example 2-3: 0.9(200) + 1.0(-104) = 76), otherwise they add the toward value. Every load is typed positive.
